notes: Fix for the single-use port error: the Nano's 3.3V pin and the red jumper (wire5) both appeared on hole 62b.j. A hole holds one lead, so wire5 now goes into 62b.i. That hole is on the same column strip (62b, rows f-j), so the electrical connection is the same.

Breadboard coordinates are read from the Fritzing image. Rows a-e (the lower half in the picture) are bank 't'. Rows f-j (the upper half) are bank 'b'. The Nano's upper pin row is at row j. Its lower pin row is at row e. The two bottom rails are 'bp' (positive, red line) and 'bn' (negative, blue line). Rail hole numbers are the nearest column number.

The manual and image do not say which Nano pins are used. I assumed 3.3V for the top-right pin, which the red wire takes to the + rail. I assumed GND.1 for the pin in column 51, which the black wire takes to the - rail. I picked D2 for the IR receiver data pin and D3 for the IR LED drive pin. Check these against the sketch.

Only the Nano pins that matter to the circuit are listed as joined to the breadboard. The Nano physically plugs into every hole along its two rows. In the image the blue wire and the resistor sit on the strip of column 49, which also holds a Nano pin. I did not model that pin.
The IR receiver legs from left to right are VCC (column 31, red wire to + rail), GND (column 32, black wire to - rail) and DAT (column 34, green wire to the Nano). This matches the usual pin order.

The IR LED is the 'IR transmitter'. Its straight leg (cathode) is in column 43 and goes to the - rail. Its bent leg (anode) is in column 44 and goes to the 330 ohm resistor. The other end of the resistor, in column 49, goes by the blue wire to the Nano pin in column 60.
The Arduino Cloud, Alexa skill and sketch steps are software only, so they add no nodes or edges. The Nano is powered over USB, which the image does not show.
